testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Do not push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force of springs and air pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check slack adjusters after parking and setting wheel chocks. Pull each adjuster to check movement. It should move no more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it is out of adjustment and needs repair.

questions.question: When traveling down a steep downgrade:

options.text: The air brakes should be used.
The vehicle should be placed in a low gear and the driver should use engine braking.
The driver should continually downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should be placed in a low gear and the driver should use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downgrades, use engine braking to control your speed. Use the brakes only to help with engine braking.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks, but only if you have applied the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When parked on a level surface, use wheel chocks. This is especially important if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: While driving, ____ generally holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: What kind of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.explanation: During inspection, park on level ground and set wheel chocks. Pull each slack adjuster to check movement. It should move no more than one inch. If it moves more, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within ____ seconds.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should reach 85 to 100 psi in both tanks within about 45 seconds.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving, but continue driving if nothing seems wrong.
Drive with the hazard lights activated.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. You need to stop while you still have some braking power left.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank prevents air from escaping if the air compressor has a leak.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It keeps air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: The emergency brake system is made up of ____.

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three different braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: If the brakes produce too much heat:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual

questions.explanation: Brakes are made to handle heat, but do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. If brakes get too hot, they may fade and lose their ability to slow the vehicle. Also use engine braking.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using the brake pedal at the same time could damage the brakes by putting too much force on them.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the proper control releases the spring brakes for a short time so the driver can move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a slope

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Brakes can lose adjustment quickly, especially when they are:
questions.explanation: Brakes lose adjustment quickly when they are hot. Check your brake adjustment regularly. All brakes must be properly adjusted and working for safe vehicle control.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels and located on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are found inside the brake drum.

questions.question: What does an alcohol evaporator do in an air brake system?

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Stops ice from forming in the brake system.
Lubricates parts of the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol into the system. The alcohol prevents ice from forming inside the brake system.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air storage tanks?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They store compressed air for the brakes.
They should be emptied of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They store compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air that powers the brakes in an air brake system. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, governor, storage tanks, drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, pressure gauges, warning signals, stop light switch, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of the brake system.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob outward to apply the brakes and push it inward to release them.
